response.reason: NL1 is purely descriptive context introducing the model subject with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes a continuous pre-completion task (target search), a cardinality obligation over three state areas, and an eventual termination concept (mission completed) that gates the continuous behavior. NL3 establishes a transition-endpoint obligation from the operating swarm scope to a formation-adjustment state triggered by interception, with an implicit containment of the formation-adjustment state as one of the three state areas. NL4 establishes a transition-endpoint obligation into an attack state triggered by task-assignment-information event, and an effect/variable-delta obligation that the swarm's UAV count decreases after completing the attack. I represent each atomic obligation separately per the atomic-contract-shape rules, project the two alternatives (interception, task assignment) as transition-group alternatives sharing an owner-level source (the continuous target-search/operating state), and preserve termination for mission completion without inventing a progress contract for termination itself while still preserving the explicit continuous state_action obligation for target search.

segment_coverage.basis: NL1 text: 'This state machine model describes the state transitions of a UAV swarm.'
segment_coverage.reason: Pure descriptive introduction naming the modeled system (UAV swarm) with no normative obligation to extract.

segment_coverage.basis: NL2 text about continuous target search across three state areas.
segment_coverage.reason: Establishes a continuous operating task (target search) prior to mission completion, and a cardinality obligation over three state areas.
unresolved_readings: Whether the three state areas are concurrent regions or direct child states remains open; NL only says the swarm 'operates within' three different state areas without explicit parallel/orthogonal language, so direct_child_states is the primary reading with concurrent_regions as an alternative only if source diagrams show regions.

segment_coverage.basis: NL3 text: 'When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.'
segment_coverage.reason: Establishes an interception-triggered transition into the formation adjustment state and its membership among the state areas.

segment_coverage.basis: NL4 text about entering attack state on task assignment information and decreasing UAV count after completing attack.
segment_coverage.reason: Establishes a task-assignment-triggered transition into the attack state, containment of attack state, and a post-attack UAV-count decrease effect.

alternatives.reason: NL3 states an exact event (interception) causing a transition from the ongoing target-search operating condition to the formation adjustment state.

alternatives.basis: NL4 text: 'During flight, if task assignment information is received, it enters the attack state.'
alternatives.reason: NL4 continues the operating narrative, stating that during flight, receiving task assignment information causes entry into the attack state; this is a second alternative from the same ongoing operating condition.

transition_groups.basis: NL2 establishes continuous target search as the ongoing operating condition; NL3 and NL4 each state a distinct event causing departure from that condition to a different named state, with no indication that formation adjustment leads into attack or vice versa.
transition_groups.reason: Both NL3 and NL4 describe alternative event-triggered transitions out of the UAV swarm's ongoing operating/target-search condition established in NL2, sharing the same continuing source scope rather than each other as sequential targets.
transition_groups.source_name: target search operating state (UAV swarm, before mission completion)

(2) NL3-ENDPOINT-1 and NL4-ENDPOINT-1 transitions exist exactly as required (TargetSearchingState->FormationAdjustmentState on Intercepted; TargetSearchingState->AttackState on Task_Assignment_Received), so these are satisfied and omitted. response.reason: This lens audits root reachability, consumer coverage, termination stability, and dead-end frontier facts. The closed FCSTM shows FormationAdjustmentState (line 8) and FinalWaittr_0006 (line 10) are reachable leaves with no outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostics, refuted deadlock checks with outgoing_count=0). The NL2 termination contract requires the mission to reach a completed/terminated condition; FinalWaittr_0006 is the modeled realization of the Mission Completed transition and is a true sink with zero outgoing edges, which is consistent with stable termination (no re-entry or cycling), so that contract is satisfied and omitted. The NL3 endpoint (TargetSearchingState->FormationAdjustmentState on Intercepted) exists exactly at transition:line:12, but FormationAdjustmentState itself is a dead-end with no way back into the operating cycle or toward mission completion, which is a distinct dead-end/consequence property from the endpoint contract itself. Since NL3-ENDPOINT-1 only requires the transition to exist (satisfied, so omitted from candidates), the dead-end consequence is best captured as a derived deadlock/progress-style obligation tied to NL2's ongoing-operation contract, but per instructions I must not invent progress contracts merely because a state is named/entered. The NL2-ACTION-1 state_action progress contract requires continuous target-search operation prior to mission completion; the FormationAdjustmentState dead-end blocks any path back to continuous target-search behavior once interception occurs, which is a genuine violation of the 'must_progress'/'not_retained' obligation over the exact leaf that the deterministic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/V1 fact closes. I bind this as a V1(initial_scope) candidate against NL2-ACTION-1 using the reachable non-final leaf FormationAdjustmentState. Event-consumer coverage for all four events (Intercepted, Task_Assignment_Received, Attack_Completed, Mission_Completed) shows declared_ref consumers with reachable_consumer_state_refs/reachable_consumer_transition_refs all non-empty and equal to declared consumers, so NL3/NL4 endpoint transitions are operationally reachable/consumed; no consumer-coverage defect exists. Root reachability: reachability_equivalent_facts show all six states reachable_from_initial=true, and the initial-entry checks (line:17 root->SearchingState, line:11 SearchingState->TargetSearchingState) are both proved; NL2-DERIVED initial-entry contract (owner=UAV swarm operating condition/SearchingState, target=TargetSearchingState) is satisfied by transition:line:11, so it is omitted. NL3-DERIVED guard_disjointness: the two alternatives from TargetSearchingState carry distinct triggers Intercepted vs Task_Assignment_Received (transition:line:12 vs line:13), which are distinguishable events, not the same condition, so no guard_disjointness violation applies; that contract is satisfied/omitted. Cardinality (NL2-CARDINALITY-1) is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate.

The predicate is null here because V1 is scoped to initial_scope roots rather than this exact locus (as explained in the candidate's own reason), which is a W-boundary limitation, not a defeat of the underlying fact. The strongest alternative -- that formation adjustment is an intentionally stable terminal condition -- is not supported by any exact NL terminal clause, formal terminal edge, or explicit terminal fact in the supplied dossier; NL only frames continuous operation, so this alternative remains a competent but unresolved-support reading that survives merely as an undercutting possibility rather than a rebuttal that defeats the violation.

issues.observed: The closed FCSTM shows FormationAdjustmentState (state:FormationAdjustmentState:line:8) as a reachable leaf state with zero outgoing transitions, per the LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic and the corroborating verify_facts deadlock check (outgoing_count=0). Once entered via interception, the swarm can never leave this state area.
issues.reason: The deterministic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/deadlock-frontier fact for a state that NL2 frames as one of three continuously-operating state areas is exactly the kind of finite deadlock-frontier evidence the routing discipline directs toward a V1(initial_scope)-eligible candidate; predicate expressiveness is limited here since V1 is scoped to initial_scope roots rather than an arbitrary leaf, so this remains a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than a silently dropped structural gap.
issues.requirement_quote: it transitions to the formation adjustment state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL text does not explicitly require formation adjustment to loop back or continue; it may be intentionally a stable terminal condition once formation is adjusted, and NL provides no explicit progress/response obligation attached specifically to this state.
issues.title: Formation adjustment state area is a structural leaf with no outgoing transition, isolating one of the three required operating state areas from continued operation

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING line 8), inspection_equivalent_facts.states (FormationAdjustmentState outgoing_transition_refs=[]), verify_facts.checks.non_proved (deadlock:state:FormationAdjustmentState:line:8, outgoing_count=0), transition:line:12 endpoint fact, contract NL-CONTRACT-NL2-ACTION-1 continuous-operation obligation.
issues.expected: The UAV swarm must continuously (ongoingly) perform target-search behavior as an operating activity prior to mission completion; any transition away from TargetSearchingState triggered during normal operation must eventually be able to resume or continue that ongoing operating activity rather than permanently halting all further state-machine progress in a reachable non-final scope.
issues.observed: transition:line:12 (TargetSearchingState -[Intercepted]-> FormationAdjustmentState) is an exact modeled transition, but FormationAdjustmentState is a reachable, non-final leaf state with outgoing_transition_refs=[] (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic at line 8; verify_facts deadlock check refuted with outgoing_count=0). Once interception occurs, the swarm can never resume target-search, never reach attack, and never reach mission completion; the ongoing operating activity required by NL2 is permanently blocked from this exact reachable frontier.
issues.reason: The deterministic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/refuted-deadlock fact on FormationAdjustmentState closes a reachable, non-final, sequential no-continuation frontier reached directly from the exact operating state governed by NL2's continuous-operation obligation; this is exactly the V1(initial_scope) frontier fact the routing discipline authorizes, not a mere named/entered state.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL only states a triggered transition on interception and does not literally require FormationAdjustmentState to have its own outgoing edge; the state_action obligation targets TargetSearchingState's own activity, and one could argue the dead-end is a separate/absent formation-recovery obligation not textually stated, so this remains a precise but registry-adjacent claim best expressed as V1 rather than a certain state_action violation.
issues.title: Interception transition routes ongoing target-search behavior into a dead-end state with no return path

NL2 establishes a continuous pre-completion task (target search), a cardinality obligation over three state areas, and an eventual termination concept (mission completed) that gates the continuous behavior. stage_receipts.reason: NL1 is purely descriptive context introducing the model subject with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes a continuous pre-completion task (target search), a cardinality obligation over three state areas, and an eventual termination concept (mission completed) that gates the continuous behavior. NL3 establishes a transition-endpoint obligation from the operating swarm scope to a formation-adjustment state triggered by interception, with an implicit containment of the formation-adjustment state as one of the three state areas. NL4 establishes a transition-endpoint obligation into an attack state triggered by task-assignment-information event, and an effect/variable-delta obligation that the swarm's UAV count decreases after completing the attack. I represent each atomic obligation separately per the atomic-contract-shape rules, project the two alternatives (interception, task assignment) as transition-group alternatives sharing an owner-level source (the continuous target-search/operating state), and preserve termination for mission completion without inventing a progress contract for termination itself while still preserving the explicit continuous state_action obligation for target search.
